To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of the barriers perceived by people living with HIV/AIDS were related to physical limitations.
The most common perceived barriers to physical activity in the sample were lack of motivation or fatigue (48.6%), lack of company (45.7%) and the presence of an injury or illness (37.1%).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the main barriers to physical activity perceived by people living with HIV/AIDS.
the identification of the barriers that prevent people living with HIV from participating in physical exercise and with the development of a program that will enable them to practice it regularly.

the analysis of the main personal barriers to the practice of physical activity identified by people living with HIV/AIDS, and the impact that the use of antiretroviral medication may have on the practice of physical exercise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study show the prevalence of personal barriers for the practice of physical activity perceived by people living with AIDS, and the main personal barriers were identified as: (1) laziness or tiredness (48.6%); ( 2) lack of companionship (45.7%); ( 3) having an injury or illness (37.1%); ( 4) lack of money and fear of getting hurt (34.3%, for both).

the use of anti-retroviral drugs for HIV/AIDS patients is a barrier to the practice of physical activity, which is a factor that should be considered in the development of interventions to promote physical activity among this population.
the use of the 3D-ECOG in the assessment of the elderly population is a reliable and valid method to evaluate the functional status.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the presence of an HIV/AIDS diagnosis is associated with an elevated prevalence of perceived barriers for physical activity.
we found that the majority of the barriers to exercise were physical in nature.
we have developed an innovative approach for the analysis of the effects of the effects of HIV on HIV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to do more work to better understand how to help individuals who experience barriers to exercise.
